ops.title: Codex desktop broker smoke blocked by workspace routing
ops.body:
STATUS: ROUTE PARTIALLY PROVED; GRAPHICAL INTERACTION BLOCKED BY APP-SERVER WORKSPACE-ROUTING CONTRACT

Scope

- Checkout source stayed read-only at /Users/yasyf/.orca/workspaces/cc-interact/codex-interact. No source files, commits, global Codex config, or global plugin caches were changed.
- The probe used /tmp/codex-port-bin/cc-codex, standalone /opt/homebrew/bin/codex 0.155.1, account home /tmp/codex-port-desktop-smoke-run-ctx_0cd582b700f4/account, and isolated Electron profiles under the same /tmp prefix.
- No Codex desktop main process was running before the first probe. The existing user app and existing threads were not opened, stopped, or targeted. The copied authorized auth.json was never printed.

Version event

- The first isolated launch started from /Applications/Codex.app 26.915.31945 build 9922 with bundled codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.9.2.
- Sparkle reported update_available and download_completed, replaced /Applications/Codex.app, and the isolated process exited. The installed app then reported 26.917.51856 build 10492 with bundled codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.16.
- This update was not requested or approved by the probe. It was reported immediately to the coordinator, who confirmed the user had been informed and directed the probe to continue against 26.917 without reverting.

Separate-instance support

- Static inspection of the shipped Electron bundle found CODEX_ELECTRON_USER_DATA_PATH is resolved and passed to app.setPath("userData"). Its single-instance predicate is packaged && (!macOS || hasExplicitUserDataPath), so a distinct explicit profile owns a distinct singleton lock rather than forwarding into a normal macOS instance.
- The launched process command included --user-data-dir=/tmp/codex-port-desktop-smoke-run-ctx_0cd582b700f4/user-data. The profile created SingletonLock pointing at the isolated PID. A second trial used a read-only clone of the existing desktop profile at /tmp/codex-port-desktop-smoke-run-ctx_0cd582b700f4/user-data-cloned; it reproduced the same routing failure without opening existing local threads because CODEX_HOME remained isolated.

Actual desktop WebSocket route

- Static support is present: the Electron app chooses process.env.CODEX_APP_SERVER_WS_URL unless CODEX_APP_SERVER_FORCE_CLI is exactly "1".
- Live process 57987 had CODEX_HOME=/private/tmp/codex-port-desktop-smoke-run-ctx_0cd582b700f4/account, CODEX_APP_SERVER_WS_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:62089, CODEX_APP_SERVER_FORCE_CLI=0, and the isolated user-data path.
- lsof showed ChatGPT PID 57987 TCP 127.0.0.1:62106 -> 127.0.0.1:62089 ESTABLISHED. The broker's canonical upstream was standalone app-server PID 57984 at ws://127.0.0.1:62080.
- Electron logged transport=websocket, Current reported app-server version: currentVersion=0.155.1, initialize_handshake_result outcome=success, and Codex CLI initialized. This proves the actual shipped graphical frontend, not a synthetic desktop-context client, connected through the new cc-interact broker to the standalone server.

Real thread/start binding

- During the real graphical launch, the desktop's ambient-suggestions path sent a native thread/start through the broker. Electron logged turn/started for conversation 01a0cda3-c92e-7b60-835b-8a3bf535f3e8.
- bridge.db recorded identity {host:codex, account_home:/private/tmp/codex-port-desktop-smoke-run-ctx_0cd582b700f4/account, endpoint:ws://127.0.0.1:62080, thread_id:01a0cda3-c92e-7b60-835b-8a3bf535f3e8}, generation 1, broker PID 57974, terminal_env {}. Registration therefore happened on the actual desktop frontend path and retained the canonical upstream identity plus desktop-empty terminal context.
- This app-created thread was not a usable persistent user thread. A later native thread/read returned -32600 "thread not loaded", and the app's deep-link lookup reported the same result.

Persistent-thread resume attempt

- A disposable persistent thread was created directly on the isolated canonical server: 01a0cdab-66a1-7bc3-b031-aa568591e525, ephemeral=false, historyMode=paginated, cwd=/tmp/codex-port-desktop-smoke-run-ctx_0cd582b700f4/work, status idle.
- The actual desktop was launched through the broker with codex://threads/01a0cdab-66a1-7bc3-b031-aa568591e525. The deep-link read no longer returned "thread not loaded", but the renderer stayed on the splash/blank shell and exited without a thread/resume. bridge.db retained only the ambient generation-1 row and never gained a binding for the persistent thread.
- /tmp/codex-port-desktop-smoke-route-block.png is the captured blank graphical window from this attempt.

Concrete blocker

- Sanitized native responses from standalone 0.155.1 were: account/read keys [account, requiresOpenaiAuth], account.type=chatgpt, workspaceRouting absent; configRequirements/read requirements had no keys.
- The shipped desktop requires account/read.workspaceRouting for app-server versions >= 0.155.0-alpha.5. Its legacy fallback applies only to versions >= 0.141.0 and < 0.155.0-alpha.5 when residency/network requirements are absent.
- Electron therefore logged "Workspace routing is unavailable for this account and app-server version", then repeated authenticated desktop request failures with status 432, including /wham/statsig/bootstrap, /accounts/check/v4-2023-04-27, /wham/tasks/list, /wham/onboarding/context, /wham/usage, and /settings/user. It also logged chatgpt-account-lookup result=failed, failureType=accounts_request_failed, authenticatedAccountPresent=false.
- Copying the existing desktop user-data profile into the isolated /tmp profile did not change the response or the failure. This distinguishes the real WebSocket route, which works, from the account/workspace contract needed to render and operate the desktop thread UI, which does not.

Unproved desktop gates

- No interactive composer became available, so no user-created graphical thread/start was possible.
- The graphical frontend never issued thread/resume for the disposable persistent thread, so a real desktop generation increment was not proved.
- No real desktop approval request could be surfaced or answered. Broker unit coverage preserves arbitrary bidirectional approval RPCs, but that is not counted as graphical evidence.
- Idle and active feedback were not injected into the app-created ambient thread because it was not persistent, and the persistent thread never acquired a desktop binding. The separate native broker smoke at /tmp/codex-interact-broker-live.log proves idle and same-turn active toolOutput delivery with model acknowledgements, but it is not counted as desktop proof.

Required follow-up

- Align the validated standalone 0.155.1 server with the desktop workspace-routing contract: either make account/read return the workspaceRouting object expected by current desktop builds, pass the missing supported account-routing input when the shared server starts, or deliberately validate a desktop/runtime pair whose legacy routing contract applies.
- Repeat this exact isolated graphical probe only after account/read contains workspaceRouting or an explicitly supported legacy pair is selected. The acceptance gate remains: visible composer; graphical user thread/start binding; graphical thread/resume generation increment; visible approval request and response; idle feedback starting work without user input; and active feedback joining the same native turn with preserved tool provenance.

Cleanup

- All probe-owned ChatGPT, cc-codex broker, and standalone app-server processes exited or were terminated. The isolated account, profiles, helper, ASAR extraction, screenshot, and this report remain under /tmp/codex-port-desktop-smoke* for inspection.
